d:
Author Jane Dougherty discusses her powerful new novel Pasiphae, a bold reimagining of one of Greek mythology’s most misunderstood queens.
Drawing on her lifelong love of mythology—shaped in part by her Irish heritage and academic background in early European medieval history and literature—Jane explores the story of Pasiphaë (Pacifi). Rather than accepting the traditional version of the myth, she examines how Pasiphaë’s story may have been distorted by later Greek writers who projected their own patriarchal values onto a much older civilization.
